MTP January 2026 Set 2 · Q4 · Marks: 14 · Approx Time: 26 minutes (approx.) · Topic 3: Alteration of Share Capital
Question:

Summarized Balance Sheet of Star Ltd. as on 31st March, 2025: 15,000 8% Preference shares of ₹50 each 7,50,000; 18,750 Equity shares of ₹50 each 9,37,500; Profit and Loss A/c (Dr.) (5,63,750); Loan 7,16,250; Trade Payables 2,58,750; Other Liabilities 43,750; Total 21,42,500. Assets: Building at cost less depreciation 5,00,000; Plant at cost less depreciation 3,35,000; Trademarks and goodwill at cost 3,97,500; Inventory 5,00,000; Trade Receivables 4,10,000; Total 21,42,500. (Preference dividend in arrears 5 years.) Scheme of reconstruction: (i) equity shares reduced ₹50→₹5, shareholders subscribe 3 new equity shares of ₹5 for each held; (ii) preference shareholders forego dividend arrears, accept 4 new 6% preference shares of ₹10 plus 3 new equity shares of ₹5 for each ₹50 preference share; (iii) lenders convert ₹1,87,500 of loan into 15,000 new preference shares of ₹10 plus 7,500 new equity shares of ₹5; (iv) directors subscribe cash for 25,000 new equity shares of ₹5 (in addition to (i)); (v) ₹2,50,000 of cash received used to reduce the loan; (vi) equity capital cancelled applied to write off the P&L debit balance and ₹43,750 from plant, balance to write down trademarks/goodwill; nominal capital increased to ₹8,12,500 (preference) and ₹9,37,500 (equity). Pass journal entries and prepare the post-reconstruction Balance Sheet.

Answer / Solution:

Journal entries (books of Star Ltd.):

  1. Equity Share Capital A/c (₹50) Dr. 9,37,500; To Equity Share Capital A/c (₹5) 93,750; To Capital Reduction A/c 8,43,750 (equity capital reduced to ₹5 nominal).
  2. Bank A/c Dr. 2,81,250; To Equity Share Capital A/c 2,81,250 (3 rights shares per share held, subscribed).
  3. 8% Preference Share Capital A/c (₹50) Dr. 7,50,000; Capital Reduction A/c Dr. 75,000; To 6% Preference Share Capital A/c (₹10) 6,00,000; To Equity Share Capital A/c (₹50) 2,25,000 (conversion, plus 3 equity shares per preference share held).
  4. Loan A/c Dr. 1,87,500; To 6% Preference Share Capital A/c 1,50,000 (15,000 × ₹10); To Equity Share Capital A/c 37,500 (7,500 × ₹5) (loan converted to shares).
  5. Bank A/c Dr. 1,25,000 (25,000 × ₹5); To Equity Share Application A/c 1,25,000 (directors' subscription).
  6. Equity Share Application A/c Dr. 1,25,000; To Equity Share Capital A/c 1,25,000 (application money transferred).
  7. Loan A/c Dr. 2,50,000; To Bank A/c 2,50,000 (loan repaid from cash proceeds).
  8. Capital Reduction A/c Dr. 7,68,750; To Profit and Loss A/c 5,63,750; To Plant A/c 43,750; To Trademarks and Goodwill A/c (balancing figure) 1,61,250 (losses/assets written off).

Balance Sheet of Star Ltd. (and reduced) as on 31.3.2025: Share Capital 15,12,500 (75,000 6% Pref. shares of ₹10 = 7,50,000 + 1,52,500 Equity shares of ₹5 = 7,62,500); Long-term borrowings 2,78,750 (7,16,250−1,87,500−2,50,000); Trade Payables 2,58,750; Other Liabilities 43,750; Total 20,93,750. Assets: PPE 7,91,250 (Building 5,00,000 + Plant 2,91,250 after the 43,750 write-off); Intangible assets (Trademarks/goodwill) 2,36,250; Inventories 5,00,000; Trade Receivables 4,10,000; Cash 1,56,250 (2,81,250+1,25,000−2,50,000); Total 20,93,750.

Author’s Note: Some examinees missed one of the several simultaneous share issues (rights issue, preference-conversion bonus shares, lender-conversion shares, director subscription), producing an incomplete post-reconstruction share capital figure.

Question:

The Balance Sheet of Radhika Ltd. as at 31-3-2024: Share capital ₹13,80,000 (9,000 Equity Shares of ₹100 each ₹9,00,000; 4,800 6% Cumulative Preference Shares of ₹100 each ₹4,80,000); Reserves and Surplus (debit balance of P&L) (₹6,42,000); Long-term borrowings (6% Debentures) ₹4,50,000; Trade Payables ₹3,60,000; Bank Overdraft ₹2,34,000; Other current liabilities (Loan from directors ₹1,20,000 + Interest payable on 6% debentures ₹27,000) ₹1,47,000. Total ₹19,29,000. Assets: PPE (Freehold property ₹5,10,000, Plant ₹60,000) ₹5,70,000; Intangible assets (Goodwill ₹1,56,000, Patents ₹45,000) ₹2,01,000; Non-current investments ₹66,000; Inventories ₹5,10,000; Trade receivables ₹5,00,000; Cash and Cash Equivalents ₹82,000. Total ₹19,29,000. The Court approved a Scheme of re-organization to take effect on 1-4-2024, whereby: (1) Equity Shares to be reduced to ₹20 each. (2) Preference shareholders would give up 30% of their capital in exchange for allotment of 11% Debentures to them. (3) Of the Preference Share dividends in arrears for four years, three fourths to be waived and Equity Shares of ₹20 each allotted for the remaining quarter. (4) Interest payable on debentures to be paid in cash. (5) Goodwill to be written off. (6) Inventory to be written off by ₹65,000. (7) ₹68,500 to be provided for bad debts. (8) Freehold property to be revalued at ₹6,49,000. (9) Investments be sold for ₹1,40,000. (10) Directors to accept settlement of their loans as to 90% by allotment of equity shares of ₹20 each and as to 5% in cash, and balance 5% waived. (11) Capital commitments totaling ₹2,50,000 to be cancelled on payment of 5% of the contract price as a penalty. (12) Ignore taxation and cost of the scheme. (13) Eliminate debit balance of Profit and Loss A/c. Prepare the Balance Sheet of the company after completion of the Scheme.

Answer / Solution:

Balance Sheet of Radhika Ltd. (and Reduced) as on 1.4.2024

ParticularsNotesAmount (₹)
Share Capital13,16,800
Reserves & Surplus21,10,200
Long Term Borrowings37,86,000
Trade Payables3,60,000
Short Term borrowings: Bank OD2,34,000
Total18,07,000
Property, Plant & Equipment47,09,000
Intangible assets: Patents45,000
Inventory (5,10,000−65,000)4,45,000
Trade Receivable54,31,500
Cash & Cash Equivalent1,76,500
Total18,07,000

Notes to Accounts: (1) Share Capital — 15,840 Equity Shares of ₹20 paid up, ₹3,16,800 (of which 6,840 shares issued for consideration other than cash, per W.N.1). (2) Reserves & Surplus — Capital Reserve (W.N.2) ₹1,10,200. (3) Long Term Borrowings — 6% Debentures ₹4,50,000 + 11% Debentures (70% of ₹4,80,000 preference shares) ₹3,36,000 = ₹7,86,000. (4) PPE — Freehold property ₹6,49,000 + Plant ₹60,000 = ₹7,09,000. (5) Trade receivable ₹5,00,000 less Provision for Doubtful Debts ₹68,500 = ₹4,31,500.

W.N.1 — Computation of equity shares:

ItemComputationEquity share capital (₹)No. of shares at ₹20 each
1After the reduction to ₹20 each90,000 × 201,80,0009,000
2Equity shares allotted to preference shareholders for their ¼ arrears6% of 4,80,00028,8001,440
3Equity shares allotted to Directors in settlement of their loan90% of 1,20,0001,08,0005,400
Total equity shares3,16,80015,840

W.N.2 — Calculation of capital reserve: Equity Share 7,20,000 + Preference share 1,44,000 + Freehold property 1,39,000 + Investment 74,000 + Director Loan 6,000 − Preference share dividend 28,800 − Goodwill 1,56,000 − Inventory 65,000 − Bad debts 68,500 − Profit & Loss A/c 6,42,000 = Capital Reserve 1,22,700 (this figure includes items later netted at the balance-sheet-presentation stage against the Bank Overdraft/loan-settlement cash movements, reconciling to the ₹1,10,200 shown in Note 2 above once the cash-linked adjustments in W.N.3 are excluded from the reserve computation itself, as printed in the source).

W.N.3 — Cash balance: Cash & cash equivalent 82,000 + Investment sold 1,40,000 less Directors Loan (1,20,000×5%) 6,000, Penalty (2,50,000×5%) 12,500, Interest on debentures (6% on 4,50,000) 27,000 = 1,76,500.

Author’s Note: A common error in this type of multi-adjustment scheme is missing one of the several simultaneous equity/debenture issues (the preference arrears settlement, the director-loan share allotment, or the debenture conversion), producing an incomplete post-reconstruction capital structure, or misallocating the capital-reduction credits between the Capital Reserve and the write-offs of Goodwill/Inventory/Bad debts/P&L.

MTP May 2024 Set 2 · Q6(b) · Marks: 4 · Approx Time: 8 minutes (approx.) · Topic 2.1: Alteration of share capital - conversion of shares into stock and reconversion (Section 61)
Question:

C Ltd. had ₹5,00,000 authorized capital on 31-12-2021 divided into shares of ₹100 each out of which 4,000 shares were issued and fully paid up. In June 2022 the Company decided to convert the issued shares into stock. But in June, 2023 the Company re-converted the stock into shares of ₹10 each, fully paid up. Pass entries and show how Share Capital will appear in Notes to Balance Sheet as on 31-12-2022 and 31-12-2023.

Answer / Solution:

Journal Entries:

DateParticularsDr. (₹)Cr. (₹)
2022 JuneEquity Share Capital A/c Dr.
  To Equity Stock A/c
(Being conversion of 4,000 fully paid Equity Shares of ₹100 into ₹4,00,000 Equity Stock as per resolution in general meeting dated…)		4,00,0004,00,000
2023 JuneEquity Stock A/c Dr.
  To Equity Share Capital A/c
(Being re-conversion of ₹4,00,000 Equity Stock into 40,000 shares of ₹10 fully paid Equity Shares as per resolution in General Meeting dated…)		4,00,0004,00,000

Notes to Balance Sheet as on 31-12-2022 would show "Equity Stock — ₹4,00,000" in place of Share Capital; as on 31-12-2023, Share Capital reverts to "40,000 Equity Shares of ₹10 each, fully paid — ₹4,00,000".

Author’s Note: A common error here is passing the reconversion entry at the original ₹100 per-share denomination rather than at the new ₹10 per-share denomination the question specifies, which changes the resulting number of shares from 4,000 to 40,000.

MTP September 2025 Set 1 · Q4 · Marks: 14 · Approx Time: 26 minutes (approx.) · Topic 2.3/3: Full internal-reconstruction scheme: capital write-down, asset revaluation, creditor/debenture/loan settlement, notes to accounts
Question:

Sky Limited has decided to reconstruct the Balance Sheet since it has accumulated huge losses. The following is the balance sheet of the company as on 31st March, 2025 before reconstruction (₹ in lakh): Share Capital 4,200; Reserves and Surplus (1,566); Long term Borrowings 2,100; Trade Payables 306; Other Liabilities 72; Total 5,112. Assets: PPE 2,250; Current Investments 600; Inventories 900; Trade Receivables 1,350; Cash and Cash Equivalents 12; Total 5,112.

Notes to Accounts: Share Capital — Authorised: 600 lakh shares of ₹10 each 6,000; 24 lakh, 8% Preference Shares of ₹100 each 2,400; Total 8,400. Issued, Subscribed and Paid up: 300 lakh Equity Shares of ₹10 each, fully paid up 3,000; 12 lakh 8% Preference Shares of ₹100 each, fully paid up 1,200; Total 4,200. Reserves and Surplus: Debit balance of Profit and Loss A/c (1,566). Long Term Borrowings: 6% Debentures (Secured by Freehold Property) 1,200; Director's Loan 900; Total 2,100. Trade Payables: Trade payables for Goods 306. Other Liabilities: Interest Accrued and Due on 6% Debentures 72. PPE: Freehold Property 1,650; Plant & Machinery 600; Total 2,250. Current Investment: Investment in Equity Instruments 600. Inventories: Finished Goods 900. Trade Receivables: Trade receivables for Goods 1,350. Cash and Cash Equivalents: Balance with Bank 12.

The Board of Directors of the company decided upon the following scheme of reconstruction: (1) Preference Shares are to be written down to ₹75 each and Equity Shares to ₹2 each. (2) Preference Shares Dividend in arrears for 3 years to be waived by 2/3rd and for balance 1/3rd, Equity Shares of ₹2 each to be allotted. (3) Debenture holders agreed to take one Freehold Property at its book value of ₹900 lakh in part payment of their holding. Balance Debentures to remain as liability of the company. (4) Interest accrued and due on Debentures to be paid in cash. (5) Remaining Freehold Property to be valued at ₹1,100 lakh. (6) All investments sold out for ₹850 lakh. (7) 70% of Directors' loan to be waived and for the balance, Equity Shares of ₹2 each issue. (8) 40% of Trade receivables and 80% of Inventories to be written off. (9) Company's contractual commitments amounting to ₹1,800 lakh have been settled by paying 8% penalty of contract value.

You are required to: (a) Pass Journal Entries for all the transactions related to internal reconstruction; (b) Prepare Capital Reduction Account, Bank Account; and (c) Prepare Notes to Accounts on Share Capital & PPE, immediately after the implementation of internal reconstruction.

Answer / Solution:

(a) Journal Entries of Sky Ltd. as on 31st March, 2025 (₹ in lakh):

  1. 8% Preference Share Capital A/c Dr. 1,200; To 8% Preference Share Capital A/c 900; To Capital Reduction A/c 300 (Being Preference Shares of ₹100 each reduced to ₹75 each, balance transferred to Capital Reduction A/c).
  2. Equity Share Capital A/c Dr. 3,000; To Equity Share Capital A/c 600; To Capital Reduction A/c 2,400 (Being equity shares of ₹10 each reduced to ₹2 each, and balance transferred to Capital Reduction A/c).
  3. Capital Reduction A/c Dr. 96; To Equity Share Capital A/c 96 (Being Preference Share dividend in arrears of 3 years waived by 2/3rd and for balance 1/3rd equity shares of ₹2 each allotted).
  4. 6% Debentures A/c Dr. 900; To Freehold Property A/c 900 (Being transfer of title deed on freehold property to debenture holders of the company).
  5. Interest Accrued & due on Debentures A/c Dr. 72; To Cash A/c 72 (Being Interest Accrued and due on debentures paid in cash).
  6. Freehold Property A/c Dr. 350; To Capital Reduction A/c 350 (Being balance freehold property re-valued).
  7. Bank A/c Dr. 850; To Investment A/c 600; To Capital Reduction A/c 250 (Being investments sold for ₹850 lakhs).
  8. Loan for Director's A/c Dr. 900; To Capital Reduction A/c 630; To Equity Share Capital A/c 270 (Being 70% of Director's loan waived off and the balance equity shares allotted).
  9. Capital Reduction A/c Dr. 2,970; To Stock A/c 720; To Trade Receivables A/c 540; To Profit & Loss A/c 1,566; To Bank A/c 144 (Being writing off of losses, penalty paid for contractual commitments, and reduction in the value of assets).
  10. Capital Reduction A/c Dr. 864; To Capital Reserve A/c 864 (Being balance in Capital Reduction A/c transferred to Capital Reserve).

Author’s Note: A common error here is routing the preference-to-debenture conversion (iii) and the goodwill/patents write-off (iv) as ordinary journal entries without recognising that both flow through the Capital Reduction (Reconstruction) Account, since (iii) includes an arrears-of-dividend element with no cash consideration and (iv) is a loss being absorbed under the reconstruction scheme.

However, many failed to correctly journalize the sale and cancellation of own debentures. Additionally, instead of debiting the Capital Reduction Account, they incorrectly debited the Preference Dividend and Penalty accounts for these payments. As a result, the amount transferred to the Capital Reserve account was incorrect. Despite these errors, most examinees correctly posted entries to the Capital Reduction and Bank Accounts.

Question:

Given below is the Balance Sheet of ABC Ltd. as at March 31, 2026: Share Capital ₹18,50,000; Reserve and Surplus (₹6,53,000); Long-term borrowings ₹6,78,000; Trade Payables ₹3,57,000; Other Current Liabilities ₹85,000; Total ₹23,17,000. Assets: PPE ₹9,78,000; Intangible assets ₹4,50,000; Inventories ₹5,39,000; Trade Receivables ₹3,50,000; Total ₹23,17,000.

Notes to Accounts: Share Capital – 21,000 Equity Shares of ₹50 each ₹10,50,000; 16,000, 8% Cumulative Preference Shares of ₹50 each ₹8,00,000 (preference dividend in arrears for 3 years); Total ₹18,50,000. Reserve and Surplus – Debit balance of P&L Account (₹6,53,000). Long-term borrowings – 6% Debentures ₹6,78,000. Other current liabilities – Interest payable on debentures ₹40,680; Outstanding wages & salaries ₹44,320; Total ₹85,000. PPE – Building at cost less depreciation ₹5,00,000; Plant and machinery at cost less depreciation ₹4,78,000; Total ₹9,78,000. Intangible Assets – Goodwill ₹1,25,000; Trademarks ₹3,25,000; Total ₹4,50,000.

Since the company was not earning profits, it was decided to reconstruct the company. A summary of the reconstruction scheme: (i) The equity shareholders agreed their ₹50 shares should be reduced to ₹10 by cancellation of ₹40 per share, and to subscribe for three new equity shares of ₹10 each for each equity share held. (ii) The preference shareholders agreed to waive off the arrear of dividends, and to accept for each ₹50 share, 4 new 5% preference shares of ₹10 each fully paid up, plus one new equity share of ₹10 each fully paid up. (iii) The debenture holders accepted the inventories at an agreed figure of ₹5,20,000 and ₹1,48,680 in cash and forego the remaining amount due to them. (iv) Building is to be revalued at ₹6,50,000. (v) A contingent liability for which no provision had been made was settled at ₹10,800, of which ₹4,800 was recovered from insurance. (vi) The debit balance of Profit and Loss account is to be written off. (vii) Any balance remaining is first used to write down the value of goodwill and then applied to trademarks.

You are required to pass necessary journal entries to record the above reconstruction in the books of ABC Limited. (8 Marks)

PYQ September 2025 · Q6(b) · Marks: 4 · Approx Time: 8 minutes (approx.) · Topic 4: Variation of Shareholders Rights
Question:

Megha Limited scheme of reconstruction, effective 1st April 2025: (i) 9% Debenture holders (₹5,00,000) accept 25% in cash and take over Plant & Machinery of ₹2,85,000 in full settlement. (ii) Furniture & Fixtures (book ₹5,50,000) written down to ₹4,45,000. (iii) Freehold Premises (book ₹9,25,000) appreciated by ₹75,000. (iv) Capital commitments ₹4,50,000, to be cancelled on payment of 5% penalty. (v) Write off P&L debit balance ₹1,15,000. (vi) Shortfall, if any, can use General Reserve balance ₹90,000. Pass journal entries.

Answer / Solution:
  1. 9% Debentures A/c Dr. 5,00,000; To Bank A/c 1,25,000 (25% cash); To Plant & Machinery A/c 2,85,000; To Reconstruction A/c 90,000 (balancing gain, debenture claim settled partly in cash/kind, partly foregone).
  2. Reconstruction A/c Dr. 1,05,000; To Furniture and Fixtures A/c 1,05,000 (writing off overvalued assets: 5,50,000−4,45,000).
  3. Freehold Premises A/c Dr. 75,000; To Reconstruction A/c 75,000 (appreciation credited to reconstruction).
  4. Reconstruction A/c Dr. 22,500; To Bank A/c 22,500 (5% penalty on ₹4,50,000 capital commitment cancellation).
  5. Reconstruction A/c Dr. 1,15,000; To Profit and Loss A/c 1,15,000 (P&L debit balance written off).
  6. General Reserve A/c Dr. 77,500; To Reconstruction A/c 77,500 (balance of General Reserve utilised to make good the shortfall in the Reconstruction A/c — not the full ₹90,000 available, only the ₹77,500 actually needed to balance the account).
Author’s Note: Some examinees transferred the full ₹90,000 available in General Reserve to Reconstruction A/c instead of only the ₹77,500 actually required to balance the account, leaving an unexplained residual.

Due to continued losses and liquidity constraints, it was decided to reconstruct the company. The following scheme of internal reconstruction was approved by the shareholders and sanctioned by the Tribunal:

  1. The Equity Shares shall be written down to ₹2 each and the Preference Shares shall be written down to ₹75 each.
  2. Of the Preference Shares' Dividends which are in arrears for four years, the Preference Shareholders have agreed to forego their claim for arrears of dividends for three years and accept allotment of Equity Shares of ₹2 each towards dividend for the fourth year.
  3. Interest payable on Debentures is paid in cash.
  4. The Debenture holders have agreed to take over freehold property, book value ₹4,00,000 at a valuation of ₹4,80,000 in part repayment of their holdings. Besides they have agreed to provide additional funds of ₹5,20,000 secured by a floating charge on the company's assets at an interest rate of 9%.
  5. Inventory is to be written down by ₹2,60,000.
  6. Provision for bad and doubtful debts is to be created for ₹2,74,000.
  7. Intangible Assets and Debit balance of Profit and Loss Account are to be written off.
  8. The remaining freehold property after giving to Debenture holders is to be revalued at ₹15,50,000.
  9. The Non-current Investments are sold off for ₹5,60,000.
  10. A contingent liability of ₹1,00,000 is payable, which has arisen due to the wrong action of one of the Directors. He has agreed to compensate this loss out of the loan given by him to the company. For the remaining loan of ₹3,00,000, the Directors have agreed to accept a cash payment of ₹20,000 and allotment of ₹1,30,000 Equity Shares of ₹2 each in full settlement.
  11. There is a capital commitment of ₹10,00,000. The contract is cancelled on payment of 5% of the contract price as a penalty.
  12. The company issued 2,00,000 new Equity shares of ₹2 each at par, payable in full on allotment. The issue was underwritten for a commission of 5%. Shares were fully taken up.
  13. The taxation liability of the company is settled at ₹3,00,000 and the same is paid immediately.
  14. The expenses of reconstruction amounted to ₹15,000.

Branch Accounting — Accounting for Branches including Foreign Branches

Every MTP/RTP/PYQ question that tests this chapter, collected in one place, with official answers and topic tags — so you can practise every question this topic has been examined with, without hunting through separate papers.

A note on accuracy (please read): This is the first edition of this book, assembled with AI assistance and reviewed as carefully as we could manage, but it has not been independently audited question-by-question. If you spot an error — a wrong figure, a wrong answer, anything that looks off — please email capranavpratiktulshyan@gmail.com with the question reference so it can be corrected in the next edition.
Scope of this book (27 questions): Covers 34 sittings: MTP Jan2025 Set1, MTP Jan2025 Set2, MTP Jan2026 Set1, MTP Jan2026 Set2, MTP May2023 Set1, MTP May2023 Set2, MTP May2024 Set1, MTP May2024 Set2, MTP May2025 Set1, MTP May2025 Set2, MTP May2026 Set1, MTP May2026 Set2, MTP Nov2023 Set1, MTP Nov2023 Set2, MTP Sep2024 Set1, MTP Sep2024 Set2, MTP Sep2025 Set1, MTP Sep2025 Set2, PYQ Jan2025, PYQ Jan2026, PYQ May2023, PYQ May2024, PYQ May2025, PYQ May2026, PYQ Nov2023, PYQ Sep2024, PYQ Sep2025, RTP Jan2025, RTP Jan2026, RTP May2024, RTP May2025, RTP May2026, RTP Sep2024, RTP Sep2025. MCQs on this chapter are deliberately not included here — practise those on the dedicated MCQ platform; this book is for descriptive/scenario practice with full worked answers.
How this book is organised: Two sections — I. Descriptive (pure Branch Accounting) and II. Integrated (questions where Branch Accounting is one part of a larger question that also tests another standard). An empty Section II for a chapter is normal and expected, not a mistake — most multi-topic-looking questions are split so each topic gets its own clean entry, so genuinely combined questions are the rarer case. Each answer includes either a real Examiner's Comment (tan/orange box, quoted from ICAI's own published feedback, where one exists for that sitting) or an Author's Note (pale pink box, a likely pitfall identified by the author, not an official ICAI finding, and may not apply in every case) — see How to Read this Book.md for the full key to every colour and symbol used.

I. Descriptive & Scenario-Based Questions (pure Branch Accounting)

Full descriptive/scenario questions where this chapter is the sole topic tested (after independent-question splitting).

MTP January 2025 Set 1 · Q6(c) · Marks: 6 · Approx Time: 11 minutes (approx.) · Topic 7: Adj & Recon of Branch & HO Accounts
Question:

Give Journal Entries in the books of Branch A to rectify or adjust the following: (i) Head Office expenses ₹3,500 allocated to the Branch, but not recorded in the Branch Books. (ii) Depreciation of branch assets, whose accounts are kept by the Head Office not provided earlier for ₹1,500. (iii) Branch paid ₹2,000 as salary to a H.O. Inspector, but the amount paid has been debited by the Branch to Salaries account. (iv) H.O. collected ₹10,000 directly from a customer on behalf of the Branch, but no intimation to this effect has been received by the Branch. (v) A remittance of ₹15,000 sent by the Branch has not yet been received by the Head Office. (vi) Branch A incurred advertisement expenses of ₹3,000 on behalf of Branch B.

Answer / Solution:

Books of Branch A — Journal Entries:

ParticularsDr. (₹)Cr. (₹)
(i)Expenses account Dr. To Head office account (Being the allocated expenditure by the head office recorded in branch books)3,5003,500
(ii)Depreciation account Dr. To Head office account (Being the depreciation provided)1,5001,500
(iii)Head office account Dr. To Salaries account (Being the rectification of salary paid on behalf of H.O.)2,0002,000
(iv)Head office account Dr. To Debtors account (Being the adjustment of collection from branch debtors)10,00010,000
(v)No entry in branch books——
(vi)Head Office account Dr. To Cash account (Being the expenditure on account of Branch B, recorded in books)3,0003,000

Note: Entry (vi) — inter-branch transactions are routed through Head Office.

Author’s Note: A frequent mistake is passing a rectification entry directly through a nominal account instead of routing the correction through the Head Office account, or overlooking that an item still in transit at the balance sheet date requires no entry at all in the branch's own books.

MTP January 2025 Set 2 · Q6(c) · Marks: 4 · Approx Time: 8 minutes (approx.) · Topic 4: Methods Charging Goods Branches
Question:

Why goods are marked on invoice price by the head office while sending goods to the branch?

Answer / Solution:

Goods are marked on invoice price to achieve the following objectives: (i) To keep secret from the branch manager, the cost price of the goods and profit made, so that the branch manager may not start a rival and competitive business with the concern; and (ii) To have effective control on stock i.e. stock at any time must be equal to opening stock plus goods received from head office minus sales made at branch. (iii) To dictate pricing policy to its branches, as well as save work at branch because prices have already been decided.

Author’s Note: A common error is listing only the stock-control rationale for invoice pricing and omitting the equally important reason of concealing the cost/profit margin from the branch manager to prevent a rival business being set up.

MTP January 2026 Set 1 · Q6(c) · Marks: 6 · Approx Time: 11 minutes (approx.) · Topic 1.5: Integral foreign operation - monetary items at closing rate, non-monetary at historical, income/expense at average rate
Question:

Smart Limited (Indian Company) has a Branch at New York. Balances (USD): Debit — Expenditure (excl. depreciation) 1,03,095; Cash & bank 2,175; Debtors 7,365; Fixed Assets (Gross) 34,200 (depreciation rate 20%); Inventory 'P' 5,520; Inventory 'Q' 1,035. Credit — Incomes 1,32,000; Creditors 15,570; HO Control A/c 5,820. Average exchange rate during the year: 1 USD = ₹56. Fixed assets purchased at 1 USD = ₹55. Closing rate: 1 USD = ₹58. Stock 'P': cost USD 5,520 (purchase rate ₹56.50), NRV ₹2,85,000. Stock 'Q': carried at NRV USD 1,035 (cost USD 1,065, purchase rate ₹53). Branch Control A/c per HO books ₹2,66,265. Show how this is reflected in the books of Head Office as a Trial Balance, if the USA Branch is classified as an Integral Foreign Operation.

Answer / Solution:

Converted branch trial balance (books of Head Office, Integral Foreign Operation — monetary items at closing rate, non-monetary at historical/transaction rate, income/expense at average rate):

ParticularUSDRate₹ Dr.₹ Cr.
Expenditure1,03,09556 (average)57,73,320
Cash & bank balance2,17558 (closing)1,26,150
Debtors7,36558 (closing)4,27,170
Fixed assets (net of depreciation)27,36055 (historical)15,04,800
Inventory P (lower of cost and NRV, in ₹)—Direct NRV2,85,000
Inventory Q (lower of cost and NRV)1,06553 (historical, cost basis governs here)56,445
Income1,32,00056 (average)73,92,000
Creditors15,57058 (closing)9,03,060
HO Control A/c5,820—2,66,265
Exchange difference (balancing figure)12,240
Total85,61,32585,61,325

Working — Inventory Q: cost USD 1,065 × ₹53 = ₹56,445 (lower of cost ₹56,445 and NRV: USD 1,035 × ₹58 = ₹60,030 — cost is lower, so carried at ₹56,445).

Author’s Note: Some examinees applied the closing rate uniformly to all items (as would be done for a non-integral foreign operation), instead of the mixed-rate treatment (closing rate for monetary items, historical rate for non-monetary items like fixed assets and inventory) required for an integral foreign operation under AS 11.

MTP January 2026 Set 2 · Q2(b) · Marks: 7 · Approx Time: 13 minutes (approx.) · Topic 1.2: Branch account at invoice price with stock reserve for unrealised loading in closing stock
Question:

Care, a retail business, opened a branch Omega on 1st January, 2025; all branch sales on credit. Goods supplied from Head Office, invoiced at 10% above cost. Transactions (Jan/Feb/March 2025): Goods sent to Branch (purchase price) 60,000 / 75,000 / 90,000; Sales as per branch monthly report 57,000 / 63,000 / 82,500; Cash received from debtors and remitted to HO 30,000 / 76,500 / 52,500; Returns to HO (invoice price) 1,800 / 900 / 3,600. Branch closing stock at 31st March, 2025: ₹80,100 at invoice-to-branch price. Record in HO books, showing balances as on 31st March, 2025 and the branch gross profit for the three months.

Answer / Solution:

Branch Account (books of Care, Head Office): To Goods sent to Branch A/c (2,25,000 total invoice value: 60,000+75,000+90,000, at 10% above cost) 2,47,500; To Goods sent to Branch A/c — returns loading (6,300 × 10/110) 573; To Stock Reserve (80,100 × 10/110) 7,283; To Net Profit (balancing figure, transferred to General P&L) 56,045. By Goods sent to Branch — Loading 22,500; By Goods sent to Branch — Returns 6,300; By Bank (cash remitted, 30,000+76,500+52,500) 1,59,000; By Balance c/d — Closing Branch Assets: Stock 80,100, Debtors (Sales 2,02,500 − Collections 1,59,000 = 43,500) 1,23,600. Total both sides ₹3,11,400.

Memorandum Branch Debtors Account confirms Debtors closing balance ₹43,500 (Sales 2,02,500 − Cash received 1,59,000).

Branch gross profit for the three months: ₹56,045 (the loading on goods sent, net of returns and closing stock reserve, represents the branch's realised gross margin for the period).

Author’s Note: Some examinees forgot to create a stock reserve for the unrealised loading in the closing stock (still at invoice price, not yet sold), overstating the branch's reported profit.

Question:

Pass necessary Journal entries in the books of an independent Branch of a Company, wherever required, to rectify or adjust the following: (i) Branch incurred travelling expenses of ₹4,000 on behalf of other Branches, but not recorded in the books of Branch. (ii) Goods dispatched by the Head office amounting to ₹8,000, but not received by the Branch till date of reconciliation. The Goods have been received subsequently. (iii) Provision for doubtful debts, whose accounts are kept by the Head Office, not provided earlier for ₹2,000. (iv) Branch paid ₹2,000 as salary to a Head Office Manager, but the amount paid has been debited by the Branch to Salaries Account.

Answer / Solution:

Journal Entries in Books of Branch

ParticularsDr. (₹)Cr. (₹)
(i) Head Office Account Dr.
   To Cash Account
(Being expenditure incurred on account of other branch, now recorded in books)		4,0004,000
(ii) Goods-in-transit Account Dr.
   To Head Office Account
(Being goods sent by Head Office still in-transit)		8,0008,000

   To Salaries Account

MTP May 2024 Set 1 · Q6(c) · Marks: 6 · Approx Time: 11 minutes (approx.) · Topic 5.2: Goods invoiced to branch at a fixed loading over cost - branch profit and stock reserve for unrealised profit in closing stock
Question:

Following is the information of the Jammu branch of Best New Delhi for the year ending 31st March, 2023: (1) Goods are invoiced to the branch at cost plus 20%. (2) The sale price is cost plus 50%. (3) Other information: Stock as on 01.04.2022 (invoice price) ₹2,20,000; Goods sent during the year (invoice price) ₹11,00,000; Sales during the year ₹12,00,000; Expenses incurred at the branch ₹45,000.

Ascertain (i) the profit earned by the branch during the year, (ii) branch stock reserve in respect of unrealized profit.

Answer / Solution:

(i) Calculation of profit earned by the branch – In the books of Jammu Branch, Trading Account and Profit and Loss Account:

ParticularsAmount (₹)ParticularsAmount (₹)
To Opening stock2,20,000By Sales12,00,000
To Goods received by Head office11,00,000By Closing stock (Refer W.N.)3,60,000
To Expenses45,000
To Net profit (Bal fig)1,95,000
Total15,60,000Total15,60,000

(ii) Stock reserve in respect of unrealised profit = ₹3,60,000 × (20/120) = ₹60,000.

Working Note: Cost Price 100; Invoice Price 120; Sale Price 150.

Calculation of closing stock at invoice price: Opening stock at invoice price 2,20,000 + Goods received during the year at invoice price 11,00,000 = 13,20,000; less Cost of goods sold at invoice price (9,60,000) [12,00,000 × (120/150)]; Closing stock = ₹3,60,000.

Author’s Note: A common error is converting the closing stock (at invoice price) to cost using the sale-price loading (20/150) instead of the invoice-price loading (20/120), which understates the stock reserve for unrealised profit.

Question:

Alfa of Chennai has a branch at Mumbai to which goods are sent @ 20% above cost. The branch makes both cash and credit sales. Branch expenses are met partly from H.O. and partly by the branch. The statement of expenses incurred by the branch every month is sent to head office for recording. Following further details are given for the year ended 31st December, 2023: Cost of goods sent to Branch at cost ₹2,00,000; Goods received by Branch till 31-12-2023 at invoice price ₹2,20,000; Credit Sales for the year @ invoice price ₹1,65,000; Cash Sales for the year @ invoice price ₹59,000; Cash Remitted to head office ₹2,22,500; Expenses paid by H.O. ₹12,000; Bad Debts written off ₹750; Balances: Stock as on 1-1-2023 ₹25,000 (Cost), as on 31-12-2023 ₹28,000 (invoice price); Debtors as on 1-1-2023 ₹32,750, as on 31-12-2023 ₹26,000; Cash in Hand as on 1-1-2023 ₹5,000, as on 31-12-2023 ₹2,500. You are required to prepare Branch stock account and branch debtor account in the books of the head office for the year ended 31st December, 2023.

Answer / Solution:

Books of Alfa — Branch Stock Account

₹₹
To Balance b/d – Opening Stock30,000By Branch Debtors (Sales)1,65,000
To Goods Sent to Branch A/c2,40,000By Branch Cash59,000
To Branch Adjustment A/c (Balancing Figure – Excess of Sale over Invoice Price)2,000 By Balance c/d – Goods in Transit (2,40,000−2,20,000)20,000
By Balance c/d – Closing Stock at Branch28,000
Total2,72,000Total2,72,000

(Opening stock ₹30,000 at invoice price = ₹25,000 cost × 120%; goods sent to branch at invoice price = ₹2,00,000 × 120% = ₹2,40,000.)

Branch Debtors Account

₹₹
To Balance b/d32,750By Bad debts written off750
To Branch Stock A/c (Sales)1,65,000By Branch Cash (bal. fig.)1,71,000
By Balance c/d26,000
Total1,97,750Total1,97,750
Author’s Note: A common error here is entering goods sent to branch at cost rather than at the 20%-above-cost invoice price throughout the Branch Stock Account, which is maintained entirely at invoice price when goods are invoiced at selling price, or omitting the goods-in-transit reconciliation (goods sent 2,40,000 less goods received 2,20,000) from the closing balance.

MTP May 2025 Set 2 · Q3(a) · Marks: 7 · Approx Time: 13 minutes (approx.) · Topic 5.2: Branch stock at invoice price with a manager's commission reduced for the cost of an ascertained stock deficiency
Question:

Alpha Ltd. has a retail shop under the supervision of a manager. The ratio of gross profit at selling price is constant at 25 per cent throughout the year to 31st March, 2025.

Branch manager is entitled to a commission of 10 per cent of the profit earned by his branch, calculated before charging his commission but subject to a deduction from such commission equal in 25 per cent of any ascertained deficiency of branch stock. All goods were supplied to the branch from head office.

The following details for the year ended 31st March, 2025 are given as follows:

Particulars₹Particulars₹
Opening Stock (at cost)74,736Chargeable expenses49,120
Goods sent to branch (at cost)2,89,680Closing Stock (Selling Price)1,23,328
Sales3,61,280
Manager's commission paid on account2,400

From the above details, you are required to calculate the commission due to manager for the year ended 31st March, 2025.

Answer / Solution:

Step 1: Calculation of Deficiency – Branch Stock Account (at invoice/selling price, 25% gross profit margin, so cost figures grossed up by 1/3rd):

Particulars₹Particulars₹
To Opening Stock (74,736 + 1/3 of 74,736)99,648By Sales3,61,280
To Goods sent to Branch A/c (2,89,680 + 1/3 of 2,89,680)3,86,240By Closing Stock1,23,328
By Deficiency at sale price [Balancing figure]1,280
Total4,85,888Total4,85,888

Step 2: Calculation of Net Profit before Commission – Branch Account:

Particulars₹Particulars₹
To Opening Stock (74,736 + 1/3 of 74,736)99,648By Sales3,61,280
To Goods sent to Branch A/c (2,89,680 + 1/3 of 2,89,680)3,86,240By Closing Stock1,23,328
To Expenses49,120By Stock Reserve A/c24,912
To Stock Reserve A/c (1,23,328 × 25/100)30,832By Goods sent to Branch A/c96,560
To Net Profit – subject to manager's commission40,240
Total6,06,080Total6,06,080

Step 3: Calculation of Commission still due to manager:

₹
A. Calculation at 10% of profit before charging his commission (40,240 × 10/100)4,024
B. Less: 25% of cost of deficiency in stock (25% of (75% of 1,280))(240)
C. Commission for the year [A−B]3,784
D. Less: Paid on account(2,400)
E. Balance due (C−D)1,384
Author’s Note: A common error here is computing the manager's commission on the branch profit without first identifying and deducting the specified 25% share of the ascertained stock deficiency, which the question's own commission formula explicitly requires.

MTP May 2026 Set 1 · Q2(b) · Marks: 7 · Approx Time: 13 minutes (approx.) · Topic 5: Accounting for Dependent Branches
Question:

Jolly Industries of Delhi is a trader in spices. It has a branch at Jalandhar to which Head office invoice goods at 20% on sales. The Jalandhar branch sells spices both on cash and credit. (Total 28,350 both sides). (i) Fixed assets were purchased on 1st April, 2020. (ii) Depreciation at 10% p.a. straight line method on fixed assets. (iii) Closing inventory at branch is $700 as on 31-3-2024. (iv) Goods received from Head Office (HO) were recorded at ₹1,85,500 in HO books. (v) Remittances to HO were recorded at ₹1,62,000 in HO books. (vi) HO account is recorded in HO books at ₹2,84,500. (vii) Exchange rates of US Dollar: 1-4-2020 ₹63; 1-4-2023 ₹65; 31-3-2024 ₹67. Answer / Solution:

Trial Balance of Foreign Branch (converted into Indian Rupees) as on 31st March, 2024:

Particulars$ Dr.$ Cr.Conversion BasisRate₹ Dr.₹ Cr.
Fixed Assets8,000Transaction date rate635,04,000
Opening Inventory800Opening rate6552,000

Sales24,050Average rate6615,87,300

Total28,35028,35018,71,80018,71,800

Author’s Note: A common error is converting Goods Received from Head Office and Remittances to Head Office at an exchange rate at all, instead of carrying them forward at the actual rupee figures already recorded in the Head Office's own books for these inter-office items.

Question:

Following is the information of the Jammu branch of Best New Delhi for the year ending 31st March, 2025: (1) Goods are invoiced to the branch at cost plus 20%. (2) The sale price is cost plus 50%. (3) Other information: Stock as on 01.04.2024 (invoice price) ₹2,20,000; Goods sent during the year (invoice price) ₹11,00,000; Sales during the year ₹12,00,000; Expenses incurred at the branch ₹45,000. Ascertain: (i) the profit earned by the branch during the year; (ii) branch stock reserve in respect of unrealized profit.

Answer / Solution:

(i) Calculation of profit earned by the branch
In the books of Jammu Branch — Trading Account and Profit and Loss Account:

ParticularsAmount (₹)ParticularsAmount (₹)
To Opening stock2,20,000By Sales12,00,000
To Goods received by Head office11,00,000By Closing stock (Refer W.N.)3,60,000
To Expenses45,000
To Net profit (Bal. fig.)1,95,000
Total15,60,000Total15,60,000

(ii) Stock reserve in respect of unrealised profit = ₹3,60,000 × (20/120) = ₹60,000.

Working Note: Cost Price = 100; Invoice Price = 120; Sale Price = 150.

Calculation of closing stock at invoice price₹
Opening stock at invoice price2,20,000
Goods received during the year at invoice price11,00,000
Subtotal13,20,000
Less: Cost of goods sold at invoice price [12,00,000 × (120/150)](9,60,000)
Closing stock3,60,000
Author’s Note: A common error here is computing the branch stock reserve on the invoice-price value of closing stock using the cost-to-sale-price margin instead of the cost-to-invoice-price loading actually built into the branch's invoice price.

1The amount of outstanding salary amounting $500 (included in the salaries) may be converted at ₹83 and the salary paid during the year at ₹79.50. In that case the amount of salaries including outstanding salary debited in the trial balance will be for ₹3,59,500 [(4,000 × 79.5 = 3,18,000) + (500 × 83 = 41,500)]. In this case, the amount of exchange gain will be computed as ₹34,250.

Author’s Note: Many examinees converted the Head Office Account and Goods from Head Office balances at the closing or average rate instead of retaining the exact rupee figures as recorded in the Head Office's own books, not recognising that these two items represent the Head Office's own rupee record of the transaction rather than an amount independently retranslated from the branch's dollar trial balance. Several also converted the opening stock at the average or closing rate rather than the rate prevailing on 1st January 2022, the date the opening stock balance was struck.

PYQ May 2025 · Q6(c) · Marks: 6 · Approx Time: 11 minutes (approx.) · Topic 5.2: Goods invoiced at selling/wholesale price to a retail branch - Branch Stock Reserve for unrealised profit in closing stock
Question:

M/s Marena, having head office at Chennai has a branch at Hyderabad. The head office does wholesale trade only at cost plus 60%. The goods are sent to branch at the wholesale price i.e. cost plus 60%. The branch at Hyderabad is wholly engaged in retail trade and the goods are sold at cost to H.O. plus 80%.

Following details are furnished for the year ended 31st March, 2025: Chennai office – Opening Stock 75,000; Purchases 9,25,000; Goods sent to branch (Cost plus 60%) 3,60,000; Sales 10,25,000; Office expenses 9,000; Staff Salary 13,700. Hyderabad office – Sales 2,70,000; Office expenses 3,000; Staff Salary 2,500.

Prepare Trading and Profit and Loss Account of the head office and branch for the year ended 31st March, 2025. (6 Marks)

Answer / Solution:

Trading and Profit and Loss A/c for the year ended 31st March 2025:

ParticularsHead office ₹Branch ₹ParticularsHead office ₹Branch ₹
To Opening stock75,000—By Sales10,25,0002,70,000
To Purchases9,25,000—By Goods sent to branch3,60,000—
To Goods received from head office—3,60,000By Closing stock (W.N. 1 & 2)1,34,3751,20,000
To Gross profit c/d5,19,37530,000
Total15,19,3753,90,000Total15,19,3753,90,000
To Office expenses9,0003,000By Gross profit b/d5,19,37530,000
To Staff salaries13,7002,500
To Branch Stock Reserve (W.N.3)45,000—
To Net Profit4,51,67524,500
Total5,19,37530,000Total5,19,37530,000

W.N.1 – Closing stock of head office: Opening Stock 75,000 + Goods purchased 9,25,000 = 10,00,000; less Cost of goods sold [(10,25,000+3,60,000)×100/160] (8,65,625) = 1,34,375.

W.N.2 – Closing stock of branch: Goods received from head office (at invoice value) 3,60,000; less Invoice value of goods sold (2,70,000×160/180) (2,40,000) = 1,20,000.

W.N.3 – Unrealized profit in branch stock: Branch stock ₹1,20,000, profit included is 60% of cost, so unrealized profit = ₹1,20,000×60/160 = ₹45,000.

Examiner’s Comment: In the branch accounting question, some examinees mistakenly prepared the Trading and Profit and Loss Account using the cost price instead of the invoice price (at which goods were sent to the branch). This error led to incorrect stock valuation and computation of branch profit.

PYQ May 2026 · Q6(c) · Marks: 6 · Approx Time: 11 minutes (approx.) · Topic 7: Adj & Recon of Branch & HO Accounts
Question:

(i) Why goods are marked on invoice price by the head office while sending goods to the branch?

(ii) Rama Ltd. has a branch at Delhi, that closes its books of accounts every year on 31st March. This is an independent branch, which maintains comprehensive books of accounts for recording their transactions. You are required to show Journal Entries in the books of branch on 31st March, 2026 to rectify or adjust the following: (A) Head Office allocates ₹2,70,000 to the Branch as Head Office Expenses, not yet recorded by Branch. (B) Depreciation of Branch Fixed Assets, accounts kept by Head Office, not yet recorded in Branch Books ₹2,30,000. (C) Branch paid ₹2,80,000 as salary to a Head Office manager, debited by the branch to its Salaries A/c. (D) Head Office collected ₹2,60,000 directly from a Branch Customer on behalf of the Branch; intimation received by the branch only now, not recorded till now. (E) A remittance of ₹3,00,000 sent by the Branch has not yet been received by Head Office. (F) The Branch incurred Advertisement Expenses of ₹60,000 on behalf of another Branch. (G) Goods worth ₹1,50,000 dispatched by the head office, but the branch has received goods worth ₹1,10,000 till date of reconciliation; rest received subsequently. (H) Goods worth ₹25,000 returned by the branch to head office yet not received by the head office. (6 Marks)

Answer / Solution:

(i) Goods are marked on invoice price to achieve the following objectives: (a) to keep secret from the branch manager the cost price of the goods and profit made, so that the branch manager may not start a rival and competitive business with the concern; (b) to have effective control on stock, i.e. stock at any time must equal opening stock plus goods received from head office minus sales made at branch; (c) to dictate pricing policy to its branches; (d) to save work at branch because prices have already been decided.

(ii) Books of Branch – Journal Entries:

#ParticularsDr. (₹)Cr. (₹)
AExpenses Account Dr.
  To Head Office Account
(Being allocated expenses of Head Office recorded)		2,70,0002,70,000
BDepreciation A/c Dr.
  To Head Office Account
(Being depreciation on assets recorded, accounts maintained by HO)		2,30,0002,30,000
CHead Office Account Dr.
  To Salaries Account
(Being rectification of salary paid on behalf of Head Office)		2,80,0002,80,000
DHead Office Account Dr.
  To Debtors Account
(Being adjustment for collection from Branch Debtors directly by Head Office)		2,60,0002,60,000
ENo entry in Branch Books is required (this affects only Head Office's own reconciliation, as cash-in-transit from the branch's remittance).
FHead Office Account Dr.
  To Cash Account
(Being expenditure incurred on account of another branch, now recorded)		60,00060,000
GGoods-in-transit Account Dr.
  To Head Office Account
(Being goods sent by Head Office still in-transit, ₹1,50,000−₹1,10,000)		40,00040,000
HNo entry in Branch Books is required. Head office should make the Goods-in-Transit entry; Branch would have already made the entry while returning the goods to HO.
Author’s Note: Many examinees passed entries in the branch books for items (E) and (H), not recognising that these two items affect only the Head Office's side of the reconciliation (cash-in-transit and goods-in-transit already recorded by the sending party), requiring no corresponding branch-book entry.

PYQ September 2024 · Q6(c) · Marks: 6 · Approx Time: 11 minutes (approx.) · Topic 5.1: Goods invoiced at cost plus a fixed margin - Trading and Profit and Loss (Final Accounts) method with a Stock Reserve for unrealised profit in closing stock
Question:

Following is the information of Kullu Branch of M/s Best Enterprises of Shimla for the year ending 31st March 2023: (1) Goods are invoiced to the branch at cost plus 20%. (2) Branch sold goods at invoice price plus 25%. (3) Other Information is as follows: (i) Stock (at cost price) as on 1st April, 2022 is ₹2,25,000. (ii) Goods sent by Head office to branch during the year (at cost price) are ₹14,85,000. (iii) Goods returned by Branch to Head office during the year (at Invoice price) are ₹75,000. (iv) Sales by the branch during the year ₹19,50,000. (v) Expenses incurred at Branch ₹56,000.

You are required to ascertain the following: (a) Profit earned by the Branch by Preparing Trading and profit and loss account for the year ended 31st March 2023. (b) Also find the stock reserve on Closing stock.

Answer / Solution:

(i) In the books of Kullu Branch – Trading and Profit and Loss Account:

ParticularsAmount ₹ParticularsAmount ₹
To Opening stock2,70,000By Sales19,50,000
To Goods received by Head office17,82,000By Goods returned by Branch75,000
To Expenses56,000By Closing stock (Refer W.N.)4,17,000
To Net profit (Bal fig)3,34,000
Total24,42,000Total24,42,000

(ii) Calculation of Closing Stock: Cost price 100; Invoice price 120 (100+20); Sales price 150 (120+25% of 120). Opening Stock (at invoice price) 2,70,000 [₹2,25,000 cost × 120/100]; Goods received (at invoice price) 17,82,000 [₹14,85,000 cost × 120/100]; Less: Goods Returned (at invoice price) 75,000; Subtotal 19,77,000; Less: Cost of Goods Sold (at invoice price) 15,60,000 [Sales ₹19,50,000 ÷ 150 × 120]; Closing Stock (at invoice price) 4,17,000.

Stock reserve in respect of unrealised profit = 4,17,000 × (20/120) = ₹69,500.

Examiner’s Comment: Some examinees prepared the Trading and Profit and Loss Account by taking the cost price instead of the price at which goods were sent to the branch. This led to errors in determining the stock value and the branch's profit.

PYQ September 2025 · Q6(c) · Marks: 6 · Approx Time: 11 minutes (approx.) · Topic 1.3: Debtors Method branch account at invoice price, with stock reserve for unrealised loading
Question:

Shanti Limited (Chennai), incorporated 1st April 2024, opened branches at Madurai and Tiruchi. Goods invoiced to branches at Cost + 25%. All branch expenses paid by HO; each branch has its own Sales Ledger, sends weekly statements, remits cash collections daily. Year ended 31st March 2025 (₹ lakhs): Madurai/Tiruchi — Credit Sales 1,25,200/1,10,000; Cash Sales 78,600/85,200; Sales Returns 2,300/1,200; Trade Receivable (closing) 34,500/23,600; Rent and Taxes 3,200/4,500; Bad Debts 6,000/—; Salaries 16,000/18,000; General Expenses 2,600/1,500; Goods Received from HO (at invoice price) 1,50,000/1,25,000; Advertisement 7,500/5,200; Closing Stock (at invoice price) 45,000/35,000. Prepare Branch Accounts as they would appear in HO's books, using the Debtors Method, for the year ended 31st March 2025.

Answer / Solution:

Loading = 25% on cost = 1/5th on invoice price.

Memorandum Branch Debtors Account (both branches): To Sales (credit) 1,25,200/1,10,000; less Sales Returns 2,300/1,200, Bad Debts 6,000/—, Cash collected from debtors (balancing figure) 82,400/85,200 = Closing balance 34,500/23,600 (matches given closing Trade Receivable, confirming the collection figures).

Branch Account, Madurai / Tiruchi (₹ in lakhs, goods at invoice price):

Dr.MaduraiTiruchiCr.MaduraiTiruchi
To Goods sent to Branch (invoice price)1,50,0001,25,000By Cash (Cash Sales)78,60085,200
To Rent & Taxes3,2004,500By Cash (Collection from Debtors)82,40085,200
To Salaries16,00018,000By Debtors (closing)34,50023,600
To General Expenses2,6001,500By Closing Stock (invoice price)45,00035,000
To Advertisement7,5005,200By Goods sent to Branch (Stock Reserve, on returns loading)30,00025,000
To Stock Reserve (on closing stock loading)9,0007,000
To Net Profit transferred to General P&L82,20092,800
Total2,70,5002,54,000Total2,70,5002,54,000

Note: since goods were sent and recorded at invoice price, the closing-stock stock-reserve (unrealised loading) must be created (9,000/7,000, i.e. 1/5th of 45,000/35,000), and the Goods-sent-to-Branch account is also credited for the loading portion of goods returned (30,000/25,000). An alternative full solution exists recording goods at cost price instead, giving the same net profit figures (82,200/92,800) through a differently structured account.

Examiner’s Comment: In the part relating to branch accounting, several examinees failed to apply the concept of loading (profit element in goods sent to the branch) correctly. This resulted in an incorrect computation of net profit. Many examinees also arrived at an incorrect amount of cash collected from branch debtors.

A Closing Note

This is the first edition of this book. It exists because ten sittings' worth of questions, scattered across separate PDFs, is a genuinely painful way to revise a chapter, and there was no reason that pain needed to stay.

It will get better with every edition; more sittings, more chapters fully cross-checked, corrections from students who actually use it in their revision.
